Lightweight Table 1 for Quarto and R Markdown

table1_kable.Rd

Returns a knitr::kable table with bold variable names and indented category levels, summaries, and missing rows. It needs only knitr, so it is a robust alternative to table1_flextable when PDF output has font or LaTeX problems. Footnotes are not included; print them separately with cat(x$notes, sep = "\n").

Usage

table1_kable(x, format = NULL)

Arguments

x

A nice_table1 object returned by nice_SMD_table1.

format

Output format passed to knitr::kable(): NULL (default, chosen from the document), "html", "latex", "markdown", or "pipe". With "latex", variable names use \textbf{} and levels are indented with \hspace{1em}; other formats use Markdown bold and non-breaking spaces.

Value

A knitr_kable object.

See also

table1_flextable, nice_table1-methods

Examples

if (requireNamespace("knitr", quietly = TRUE)) {
  d <- example_table1_data()
  tab <- nice_SMD_table1(d, "group", c("age", "sex"),
    group_for_SMD = c("Control", "Treatment"), notes = "short")

  ## Markdown (default outside a document)
  table1_kable(tab, format = "markdown")

  ## HTML and LaTeX targets
  table1_kable(tab, format = "html")
  table1_kable(tab, format = "latex")

  ## Print the notes below the table
  cat(tab$notes, sep = "\n")
}
#> Categorical variables: n (%) among nonmissing values. Continuous variables: mean (SD) and median (Q1, Q3). Missing: n (% of group).
#> SMD = absolute standardized mean difference (Control vs. Treatment); NE = not estimable.
